verses.text: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
"My thoughts are pressing me to answer. I feel an urgent need to speak.
I've heard a rebuke that shames me, and my understanding gives me a reply.
Don't you know how it's been from long ago, ever since humanity was placed on the earth?
The triumph of the wicked is brief, and the joy of the godless lasts only a moment.
Even if someone rises as high as heaven and their head touches the clouds,
they'll disappear forever like their own dung. People who saw them will ask, 'Where did they go?'
They'll vanish like a dream and won't be found, swept away like a vision in the night.
The eyes that saw them won't see them again. Their own place won't see them anymore.
Their children will have to seek the favor of the poor, and they'll have to give their wealth back with their own hands.
Their bones may be full of youthful strength, but that strength will lie down with them in the dust.
Wickedness may taste sweet in their mouth, and they may hide it under their tongue,
holding on to it and keeping it in their mouth as long as they can.
But the food turns sour inside them. It becomes cobra venom in their belly.
They swallow riches and vomit them back up. God forces the wealth out of them.
They suck in cobra venom, and the viper's tongue kills them.
They'll never gaze on the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and butter.
They'll have to give back what they worked for without swallowing it down. They won't enjoy the wealth they acquired.
They oppressed the poor and left them helpless. They seized houses they had no part in building.
Because their appetite never let them rest, they won't save any of the things they crave.
They left nothing they hadn't devoured, so their prosperity won't last.
At the height of their abundance, distress will overtake them. The hand of everyone in misery will come against them.
Just as they're about to fill their belly, God will rain down his fierce anger on them as they eat.
They may run from an iron weapon, only to be pierced by a bronze arrow.
They pull it out of their body, the gleaming point from their liver, and terrors fall on them.
Darkness is stored up for their treasures. A fire no one fanned will devour them and consume all that's left in their tent.
Heaven will expose their guilt, and the earth will rise against them.
Everything in their house will be swept away, carried off in the day of God's anger.
This is what God gives the wicked. It's the inheritance he has appointed for them."
